top_signals.title: Shipping Crisis Forces Asian Crude Buyers to Use Smaller Tankers
top_signals.summary: Record-high freight costs are changing the behavior of Asian buyers who are increasingly using smaller tankers and ships under long-term charter deals to pick crude oil supply, refining and trading sources tell Reuters. The costs of shipping crude oil have soared to record highs in recent weeks as the Iran war reshuffled trade routes and patterns and tied up more supertankers in inefficient and lengthy voyages and on a shuttle service to move crude through the Strait of Hormuz. top_signals.why_it_matters: Digital asset volatility and institutional crypto positioning changes.

top_signals.title: ¿Por qué el frenesí de deuda por la IA inquieta a los mercados?
top_signals.summary: Las grandes tecnológicas están gastando miles de millones para competir en IA y los inversionistas empiezan a buscar protección frente a su deuda. La preocupación está en cuánto costará esta carrera y si generará suficientes ingresos y retornos para justificar el endeudamiento (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Wärtsilä to Supply Engines for Brazil Inland Waterway Tugs
top_signals.summary: Wärtsilä will supply the engines for two new inland waterway pusher tugs being built by Brazilian shipyard Estaleiro Rio Maguari. The vessels, each of which will be powered by three Wärtsilä 20 engines, will support the river logistics operations of LHG Mining on the Paraguay-Paraná waterway.

top_signals.title: Activities of U.S. Affiliates of Foreign Multinational Enterprises, 2024
top_signals.summary: Majority-owned U.S. affiliates of foreign multinational enterprises employed 8.57 million workers in the United States in 2024, a 0.2 percent increase from 8.56 million workers in 2023, according to statistics on U.S. affiliate operations and finances released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.
